o.text: From Persian محاربه, ultimately from Arabic مُحَارَبَة (muḥāraba). Compare Turkish muharebe.
Ultimately from Proto-Turkic *ül-, *öl-č- (“measure; measure, measuring”), whence also Azerbaijani ülgü. Cognate with Turkish ölçmek (“to measure”), Chuvash виҫ (viś, “to measure”).
From izlə- (“to follow; to watch”) + yici (“-er”).
Ultimately from French épidémiologie, reinterpreted as an adjective.
Inherited from Old Anatolian Turkish آشرمق (aşurmaq). By surface analysis, aş- + -ır.

From Middle Mongol [Term?]; whence also modern Mongolian дуулга (duulga), from Proto-Mongolic *dugulga. Possibly via Chagatai دبولغه (dubulğa), توبولغا (tubulğa) (→ Uzbek dubulgʻa), unless the fortition of /-v~w-/ to /-b-/ was an independent development in Azerbaijani.
Compare also Old Anatolian Turkish توغلقه (toğulga, tuğulga), Ottoman Turkish توولغه, تولغه, تولقه, تغلغه, توغلغه, Kazakh дулыға (duwlığa), Kyrgyz туулга (tuulga), Southern Altai туулга (tuulga), Kumyk давулгъа (dawulğa).
The Mongolic terms is likely a Turkic borrowing itself, compare Karakhanid تُوغْلُغْ (tuğluğ), Old Turkic [script needed] (tuğluğ, tuğlığ), a derivation from Old Turkic [script needed] (tuğ, “tug, horse tail hairs”).
